subject: Social Science
central_question: How do farming systems, cropping seasons, crop requirements and reforms shape Indian agriculture?
in_scope_units: Importance of agriculture and its role in food, industry and exports.
Types of farming: primitive subsistence, intensive subsistence, commercial and plantation farming.
Cropping pattern: rabi, kharif and zaid seasons.
Major crops: cereals, millets, pulses and maize with their conditions and regions.
Food crops other than grains, beverage crops, horticulture, non-food and fibre crops.
Technological and institutional reforms, farmer support schemes and the Bhoodan-Gramdan movement.
banned_topics: Detailed soil classification from Resources and Development.
Detailed industrial location of agro-based industries from Manufacturing Industries.
Detailed irrigation-project debates from Water Resources.

known_pitfalls.claim: Plantation farming is a form of subsistence farming.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter identifies plantation as a type of commercial farming in which one crop is grown on a large area for the market and processing industries.

known_pitfalls.claim: Rice is always a subsistence crop.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter states that rice is commercial in Haryana and Punjab but can be a subsistence crop in Odisha.
The chapter states that the listed pulses are leguminous and restore fertility except arhar.
The chapter includes institutional reforms, credit, insurance, price support, information services and land movements as well as technology.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 1(i) to identify plantation agriculture from its defining feature.
Use NCERT Exercise 1(ii) to distinguish rabi crops from kharif crops.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(i) to connect a beverage crop with geographical conditions.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(ii) to write a structured answer on conditions required for rice.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(i) to organise government initiatives for higher agricultural production.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with “EXERCISES”, Questions 1 to 3, followed by project work and an agriculture word-search activity.
